newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Bearish on fewer Saudi imports.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Bearish on fewer Saudi imports.

text.p: Pressure to narrow the mogas/naphtha is returning as bearish sentiment creeps into the gasoline market, amid the absence of buyers and with talk of fewer Saudi imports, traders said on Monday.

April gasoline swaps were bid/offered at $27.20/$27.70 per barrel, much lower than the physical offer for 95-octane unleaded at $29.20 per barrel fob Singapore lifting March 25-April 9. Unleaded 92-octane for the same timing was also offered at $28.80, up five cents from Friday's deal level.
But no buyers emerged and the strength in the prompt naphtha started to put pressure on the mogas/naphtha spread, traders said.
Sentiment on April gasoline was also bearish on news that Saudi Aramco might not buy as much as 1.5 million barrels of 95-octane leaded gasoline it tendered for in April.
Traders said the national oil company was shocked at the high c-and-f Ras Tanura offer of $6-$8 per barrel over Singapore naphtha fob quotes, and was planning to buy less than a million barrels.
The tender closed March 4 and is valid until March 12.

Gulf-based traders said Aramco's appearance in the spot market for such a large volume of petrol was to meet the demands at next month's annual pilgrammage in the kingdom, at a time domestic output was being crimped by higher exports of naphtha.
Aramco regularly imports gasoline from neighbouring Bahrain under a term contract and occasionally enters the spot market to cover shortfalls, traders said.
The backwardation in the naphtha market widened amid healthy demand for prompt cargoes, traders said.
They said buyers were still looking to cover prompt April requirements with premiums assessed around $1.00 per barrel over Singapore spot quotes, fob.

The backwardation on April/May paper widened to 60 cents per barrel from 45 cents on Friday. April was last quoted at $23.00/$23.20 and May at $22.40/$22.60 compared to Friday's quotes at $22.60/22.80 and $22.15/$22.35.
